To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) BRCA1/2 mutation carriers have an increased lifetime risk of breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and male breast cancer; (ii) TP53 germline mutation carriers have an elevated risk for breast cancer and other cancers; and (iii) the lifetime risks of breast cancer and ovarian cancer in women with a family history of breast cancer are increased.

1) genetic predisposition syndromies are a rare but important consideration in the management of patients with breast cancer; 2) genetic testing provides a powerful risk stratification tool for patients with breast cancer and those at high risk for developing breast cancer; 3) the genetic test results should be interpreted within the context of the family history; 4) genetic counseling is an important first step in the evaluation process; 5) there are multiple options for managing the risk of cancer in mutation
Genetic testing is recommended for all women with breast cancer, regardless of age or family history of cancer, to help determine their risk of developing additional primary tumors.
